clue.text: No talking in Hanover Square

indicators.note: talking means the German word is spoken, and what is heard is a different English word

parts.note: in Hanover, a German city, the word for no is nein

explanation.surface: A demand for silence posted in a square in Hanover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Hanover' tells you to put 'No' into German, NEIN; said out loud it gives the number. 'Square' looks like part of a place name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a perfect square number, being three multiplied by three.

clue.text: Steal from Polish characters drunk on flight after vacation

indicators.note: someone drunk is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of the word polish are the material to rearrange

indicators.note: a word after vacation has been emptied of its insides, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Drunken Poles misbehaving on a flight once the plane has been vacated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is not about Poland: its letters are rearranged. Emptying 'flight' leaves its first and last letters, F and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoplift is to steal goods from a shop while pretending to be a customer.

clue.text: Commotion behind the Guardian

parts.note: a behind is the backside or bottom, the rump
the newspaper refers to itself as us, so the Guardian is US

explanation.surface: A fuss going on behind the scenes at the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Guardian puzzle the paper calls itself 'us', so 'the Guardian' gives US.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance or uproar, a commotion.

clue.text: Side finally leading game — having changed side, won again

indicators.note: game here means willing to try anything, so the letters are ready to be reworked
finally points to the closing letter of the word side
the left side, L, is swapped for the right side, R, in the word leading

parts.note: taken as written before the swap

explanation.surface: A sports team, leading at the end, switch ends and win the rematch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having changed side' turns LEADING into READING by swapping L (left) for R (right); 'finally' gives E from 'Side'; 'game' then rearranges E and READING.
explanation.definitionFit: To have regained something is to have won it back after losing it.

clue.text: Joy needs to pull a man

parts.note: to heave is to pull or haul with great effort
in chess the knight, a chess man, is written N

explanation.surface: Happiness depends on picking up a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a man' is a chess piece: the knight, abbreviated N.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is used for a state of supreme happiness, as in being in seventh heaven.

clue.text: Stones' No 1, covered by Prince

definitions.note: possessive form: the stones belong to it, as in the stones of a hailstorm

indicators.note: covered by means the single letter sits inside the name, which wraps it

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
number one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stones number one hit covered by the singer Prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' is not the band but hailstones; 'No 1' is the numeral I placed inside HAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail falls as small balls of ice called hailstones, so the stones are its own.

clue.text: Lacking humour, though mostly funny

parts.note: wit is humour or cleverness with words

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are muddled
mostly means the word is cut short, losing its final pair of letters

parts.note: the full conjunction before shortening

explanation.surface: A dour person with no sense of humour, though occasionally amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last two letters of 'though', and 'funny' rearranges what is left to give HOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Without means lacking or not having, as in coming without money.

clue.text: Doctor reveals more than 2 or 3?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor discloses that a patient has more than two or three ailments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is the instruction to rearrange 'reveals'.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means a number beyond two or three but not many, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Keen to go quietly

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to urinate, to wee
p is the musical mark piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Eager to slip away without a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective meaning eager, but it is the verb to wail; 'to go' is the polite euphemism for using the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief, which is a way to cry.

clue.text: From earliest times, the odd vampire left behind one blood group

indicators.note: behind means the left abbreviation trails after the blood group letter
odd means strange, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: A is one of the blood groups

explanation.surface: An ancient vampire leaves a victim of one blood type behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the odd vampire' suggests an unusual monster; 'odd' actually shuffles its letters into PRIMAEV. 'behind' puts the left letter after the blood group.
explanation.definitionFit: Primaeval describes the very first ages of the world, so it means from earliest times.

clue.text: Politician into initially inept football team? They're getting better

indicators.note: into says the politician goes inside the combined letters
initially points to the opening letter of inept

parts.note: Rovers is a common name for a football club, such as Blackburn Rovers or Bristol Rovers
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician joins a hopeless football side, trying to improve it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts the politician after the first letter of 'inept' and before the team. Many British football clubs are called Rovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who are getting better are improving, so they are improvers.

clue.text: Not even Bale is Wales' last scorer

indicators.note: not even means only the odd-numbered letters of Bale are kept
last means the final letter of the word Wales

explanation.surface: Gareth Bale is not Wales' last scorer, a footballer's record.
explanation.walkthrough: Gareth Bale is a Welsh footballer, which makes 'scorer' look like a goalscorer. Here it means a composer of film scores: Sir Arthur Bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss was an English composer who wrote film scores, a scorer of music.

clue.text: Region's flora and fauna in book by Greek character

parts.note: iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A local plant and wildlife guide in a book by a Greek writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Biota is the collective term for the living things, plants and animals, of a region.

clue.text: One writing grand, fine novel — one with cutting edge

parts.note: a pen is something that writes
K, for kilo, is slang for a thousand pounds, a grand

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters get a fresh order

explanation.surface: An author with a fine new novel worth a grand, a cutting-edge writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' is a thousand, abbreviated K; 'novel' rearranges FINE into NIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folding knife has a blade, an object with a cutting edge.

clue.text: Idiot box broadcast ideas for fantastic state of happiness

parts.note: a fool is an idiot
to spar is to box in practice

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Idiot box, the television, broadcasting ideas for a fantasy of happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idiot box' looks like one phrase for a TV, but splits into two pieces; 'broadcast' scatters the letters of 'ideas' to give ADISE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a happiness based on illusion, so it is a state of fantasy contentment.

clue.text: Regularly looks at TV series

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is picked, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps watching television serials.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost was an American television drama about plane crash survivors on a mysterious island.

clue.text: Almost hit daughter coming out of one's shower?

indicators.note: almost means the word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to clout is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A parent nearly strikes a daughter as she steps out of the shower.
explanation.walkthrough: The shower is not a bathroom one: it is one who showers rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain cloud lets rain fall, making it a shower in the sense of something that showers.

clue.text: Credit Leavers? No question, they're animals to US

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: no means the abbreviation for question is removed

parts.note: quitters are people who leave or give up

explanation.surface: People leaving their credit cards behind, no questions asked, are beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: QUITTERS loses QU (question) to leave ITTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Critter is American slang for a creature, any animal.

clue.text: Some wind from bared US bums

indicators.note: bared means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a hobo is an American tramp or bum

explanation.surface: Wind breaking from bare American backsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bums' are not bottoms here but vagrants, which in America are hoboes.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument, one member of an orchestra's wind section.

clue.text: Wherein one gets stoned — awful dump, I gathered

definitions.text: Wherein one gets stoned — awful dump, I gathered

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a dreadful drug den where people get high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges ONE, DUMP and I together; the whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug den where people smoke the narcotic is a dump where one gets stoned.

clue.text: See 14
Here Norse gods need a second pullover

parts.note: split as pull over: pull is drag, and over turns that word backwards

explanation.surface: Norse gods here need a second jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pullover' looks like a jumper but reads as two words: 'pull' is DRAG and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology Asgard is the realm where the Aesir gods live.

clue.text: Winter sportsmen not right as weather forecasters?

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is left out

parts.note: skiers take part in winter sports

explanation.surface: Skiers who got the weather wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the sky does not forecast weather but shows what is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: The look of the sky foretells the weather, so the heavens are playful forecasters.

clue.text: Explicit communication by film group

parts.note: a sext is a sexually explicit text message
ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A racy message sent by a film group.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six, usually musicians.

clue.text: Number 4 scores with a boundary

parts.note: a score is twenty, so four scores is eighty
in cricket a six is a boundary hit clearing the rope without bouncing

explanation.surface: A cricketer, number 4 in the order, scoring with a boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 4' looks like a batting position, but 'Number' is the definition. A cricket boundary scores four or six runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighty-six is a whole number, eighty plus six.

clue.text: Like anteaters and armadillos, say, heading off to back garden?

indicators.note: to back means this piece comes behind the garden

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: Anteaters and armadillos heading off to the back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is not a mere example marker but a verb meaning state; 'heading off' removes its first letter to give TATE, and 'to back' puts that behind the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentates are an order of mammals lacking front teeth, including anteaters, sloths and armadillos.

clue.text: Team playing in China

indicators.note: playing means the letters are toyed with and moved about

explanation.surface: A sports team on tour in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: China is rhyming slang for a friend, from china plate.

clue.text: See 21
Tesla faults annoying children?

parts.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
errors are faults or mistakes

explanation.surface: Faults in Tesla cars that are irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tesla' suggests the car maker, but here it is the physics unit, symbol T.
explanation.definitionFit: Little terrors are naughty or troublesome youngsters.

clue.text: Interval drinks? Event has bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds in, so the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: Drinks at the interval of an event that serves bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interval' looks like a theatre break, but it is a musical interval.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a seventh is the interval spanning seven notes of a scale.
